fact: Xalam Analytics' January 2026 brief describes the Central African Backbone project as ongoing to expand Congo's fibre backbone, connecting to secondary towns and neighbouring countries; the brief gives no date for the work beyond its own January 2026 publication, taken as the date.

On 6 February 2023 the Central African Republic inaugurated its national fibre backbone and its interconnection with the Republic of Congo (via Bomassa), part of the 935 km of installed and operational fibre under the AfDB and EU supported Central African Backbone project, with a Congolese telecoms ministry representative present; the release says this component completes the Cameroon and Congo components.
Under the World Bank-financed Central African Backbone, Congo has been interconnected to Gabon since 2018, operated commercially since 2019 by Mambs Services, the Treasury sheet says.
The Treasury sheet says Congo has been connected to Cameroon through the CAB project since 2022.
